goals: mechanistic: quantify how soil clay content controls the partitioning of precipitation between surface runoff and deep drainage/recharge, all else fixed
key_processes: unsaturated hydraulic conductivity and its dependence on texture
deep drainage / recharge to the water table
soil-moisture storage and its seasonal cycle

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM natively partitions incoming water into surface runoff (QOVER/QRUNOFF) and sub-surface drainage/recharge (QDRAI); soil texture is a first-class per-column lever. A controlled uniform-soil sweep isolates the clay effect exactly.

answerable: clay control on surface-runoff vs deep-drainage partitioning under fixed forcing
shape (monotonicity/curvature) of the partitioning response across 5-55% clay

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 6 clay levels evenly span the requested 5-55% range; enough to resolve the expected nonlinear (steepest at low-mid clay) runoff-up/recharge-down response without wasted runs. All other properties held identical, so each level is one treatment column.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: controlled / not spatial — one representative CONUS location and one forcing window shared by all columns; only clay fraction differs.
sampling_strategy.replication: none — deterministic model, controlled treatments; replication adds no information here.

sampling_plan.reason: high-conductivity end-member: expected maximum recharge, minimum runoff — anchors the low-clay end of the response curve.
low-clay loam; samples the steep early part of the texture-conductivity response.
mid-range loam; resolves curvature in the partitioning transition.
low-conductivity end-member: expected maximum runoff, minimum recharge — anchors the high-clay end of the curve.

validation_design.observation_source: physical expectation / pedotransfer & Richards-flow theory (no in-domain observations provided)
validation_design.comparison: analog — qualitative check that response is monotonic (runoff increasing, recharge decreasing with clay) and consistent with hydraulic-conductivity theory; no co-located field data
validation_design.metric: sign and monotonicity of partitioning trend; magnitude of runoff fraction shift across clay range
validation_design.n_validation_points: 0 — conceptual experiment, validated against expectation only

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: synthetic uniform soil, clay varied 5-55% (sand+silt rebalanced at fixed ratio), single representative CONUS forcing window, identical layering/vegetation, with spin-up

requires_capabilities.capability: model spin-up (multi-year) or WTD-informed warm start
requires_capabilities.why: recharge/drainage is a slow state; cold-start at default ~8.8 m water table makes QDRAI an initialization artifact
requires_capabilities.blocks: credible recharge partitioning — the primary output

requires_capabilities.capability: synthetic uniform-soil column configuration with prescribed clay fraction
requires_capabilities.why: controlled sweep needs texture set directly (not sampled from SSURGO), varying clay while holding all else fixed

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff and drainage flux history output (QOVER/QRUNOFF, QDRAI)
requires_capabilities.why: these are the partitioning targets to be reported

assumptions: Clay cannot vary in isolation; sand and silt are rebalanced at a fixed ratio as clay changes, so the sweep is a clay-vs-(sand+silt) axis.
A single representative CONUS location and one multi-year forcing window (within 1980-2018) adequately exercise a range of storm intensities and a full seasonal wet/dry cycle.
Soil is vertically uniform (single texture through the profile) to keep the treatment clean.
Vegetation, layering, slope and all non-texture parameters are held at fixed defaults across all six columns.
Spin-up length is sufficient to bring drainage/storage to quasi-equilibrium before the analysis window.
open_questions: Preferred forcing location and window (climate regime strongly conditions the absolute runoff/recharge split)?
Should sand:silt be held at a fixed ratio, or should sand be held constant and only silt traded against clay?
Report partitioning as long-term water-balance fractions, or also resolve seasonal/event-scale behavior?
Warm-start via Fan-2013 WTD vs explicit multi-year spin-up — which is preferred given the idealized soils?
